Point at the TV. When it reacts (turns off or volume drops), press STOP / SAVE. If the code already moved on, use 1 BACK and TEST.

The TV reacted! Now each code of that batch is tried one by one (every 2.5 s). When the TV turns back on, press STOP / SAVE again.
Choose a mode and press Start

Sending burst... Watch the top LED through another phone\'s camera
Pick your brand or type a code: 001–038 brands, %1$s–%2$s universal library
AUTO per protocol: NEC 38k, Sony 40k, Philips 36k, Panasonic 37k
• Patience is key: universal setup may require trying several methods or codes. If the first one does not respond, try the next method.
• Direct line of sight: always keep a clear line between the top IR emitter of your %1$s and the TV receiver.
• Test every function: after pairing, try Power, VOL+, VOL-, CH and Menu to confirm full compatibility.
Tap the remote\'s screen and pick your brand (1: LG, 2: TOSHIBA/JVC, 3: TCL/KONKA, 4: SHOWNIC, 5: HAIER, 6: SAMSUNG, 7: PHILIPS, 8: SONY, 9: PANASONIC, 0: SHARP). The LED blinks 3 times.
Tap the remote\'s screen and type the code: 001–038 brands and Chinese boards, 101 and up the universal library.
In SEARCH pick the VOL− mode: each code sends volume bursts. As soon as the volume bar appears on screen, press STOP / SAVE.
Pause the search and use 1 BACK and TEST to step code by code while watching the TV. When it responds, save.
Press SET or SEARCH. The scanner goes through every library code, each with its real protocol and carrier. Press STOP / SAVE when the TV turns off.
The chosen code is saved automatically and kept when the app closes.

Roku IP. The phone must be on the same network. On the Roku: Settings → System → Advanced system settings → Control by mobile apps → Network access → Permissive.
Fire TV IP. The phone must be on the same network and the Fire TV must have ADB debugging on (My Fire TV → Developer options).
The Roku blocks Wi-Fi control: set Network access → Permissive in Control by mobile apps
